headline: Meta ends AI usage grading for employee performance reviews
summary: Meta previously incentivized AI tool use, leading to "tokenmaxxing." Now, performance will focus on impact, not AI adoption metrics.
details: Meta is formally ending its "tokenmaxxing" incentive program for employees. Performance evaluations will no longer depend on how much they use AI tools, according to an internal announcement this week. This reverses a policy that graded workers on their "AI-driven impact."

Almost a year ago, Meta had stated workers would be graded on their "AI-driven impact." Usage correlated with employees receiving labels such as "AI Native" or "AI First," according to a lawsuit filed by employees alleging discrimination.

New guidance replaces references to evaluating employees based on criteria like "usage of AI" with looser wording. It caveats that "these outcomes can be supported by AI or other means," restoring focus to impact regardless of how it's achieved.

Some Meta employees welcome these subtle changes, feeling freed from pressure to use AI when it doesn't make sense. Meta spokesperson Tracy Clayton confirmed the updates aim to emphasize contributions, not AI adoption dashboards or token counts.

For months, some Meta employees prompted AI tools repeatedly, or frivolously, to maximize internal usage measurements like token consumption. This "tokenmaxxing" era even saw an internal leaderboard tracking AI use, which was later taken down.

Despite these changes, Meta is encouraging, but not requiring, employees to test its new agentic AI tool known as Hatch. Similar to OpenClaw, Hatch can autonomously browse the web and operate other applications, ahead of an expected public release.

Some employees are hesitant to connect Hatch to personal accounts due to privacy worries and the possibility of errors. Past projects tracking keystrokes for AI training had previously eroded trust in the company's AI tools.

No longer fearing performance penalties for not using AI could boost morale and rebuild trust among Meta's workforce. Employees are already embracing Hatch for personal appointments and organizing life outside of work, finding it effective.

However, Hatch still consumes more tokens than standard chatbots and coding assistants. Employees believe management still expects them to effectively wield AI tools, and some fear additional job cuts if Hatch significantly boosts productivity.
